summary: Add a bounded second eval round that perturbs already-defined failure invariants across terse free text, acknowledgement ambiguity, systemic-drift pressure, epistemic compression, false assurance and evidence availability. Require multiple independent fresh-instance trials and evidence-backed classification of failures as model-behavior, grader or system-control-gap before any Core fix.

requirements.rationale: Round 2 tests robustness of existing requirements under perturbation; it promotes no new requirement.

issues_findings.rationale: The first empirical round is extended from one-off fresh runs to a bounded multi-trial robustness plan with explicit failure classification.

risks.rationale: The perturbations target continuity, systemic drift, epistemic integrity, authority and false-assurance risks already present in the canonical risk model.

decisions_concepts.rationale: Round plans and failure classification remain test/eval evidence under tests/evals; they do not create a new canonical concept or decision registry.

derived_views.rationale: The generated current-state reconciliation pointer must identify the current material eval slice. No new canonical source is introduced.

active_work.rationale: The next active proof is now a bounded 30-trial perturbation round. A failed trial must be classified with evidence before repair or Core changes are considered.
